_meta.description: Live macro themes affecting currencies but not on the scheduled news calendar. Update as regime-changing events happen. Scanner reads this at brief generation time and displays it in the daily/weekly review.
_meta.howToUse: Each theme should include: (1) short title, (2) start date, (3) currency implications with brief reasoning, (4) a specific watchLevel that would invalidate the theme, (5) affectedPairs for scanner correlation. Retire themes by moving to _retired[] with an endDate.

themes.title: Canada-US trade war live — Sep 8 retaliation in effect, Trump federal-contracts ban, oil pulled back to ~$94 widening USDCAD upside; Jan 1 2027 50% auto tariff threat structural; BoC Oct 28 next binary
themes.summary: As of September 21, the Canada-US trade war remains structurally unchanged from the Sep 8-9 escalation peak, and the key commodity variable — oil — has now shifted in a CAD-negative direction. Canada's C$27.6 billion, 700+ tariff-line retaliatory package (rates of 15%, 25%, and 50% matched dollar-for-dollar to US Section 338 and Section 232 tariffs, including doubling steel and aluminum duties to 50%) remains live since 12:01 a.m. September 8. Trump's federal-contracts ban on Canadian-origin products remains unrevoked and no diplomatic channel has been opened. The critical commodity development this week is that WTI crude surged to approximately $106 mid-week on Houthi strikes against Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline and broadening Middle East supply disruption — with Saudi Aramco informing European customers it would be unable to supply crude next month — before pulling back sharply to approximately $93.93 as of the September 21 close as Saudi crude transfers via Oman partially eased fears of a complete export halt. Hormuz traffic remains constrained and diesel supplies remain tight, leaving oil structurally supported but off the extreme highs. The pullback in oil from $106 to ~$94 is a CAD headwind: the prior $100+ oil level was actively capping USDCAD near 1.3837; a sustained move toward $90-92 would remove the primary offset against tariff-war CAD negativity and open the 1.3900-1.4017 targets. Canadian August employment printed -41,700 (vs +15,000 expected), confirming real labor market damage from the tariff war. The Bank of Canada held at 2.25% on September 2; the BoC October 28 meeting is the next critical binary — with labor deteriorating but tariff pass-through keeping inflation elevated, the BoC faces a stagflationary dilemma that could produce a dovish surprise cutting CAD further. The structural Jan 1, 2027 threat of 50% tariffs on all Canadian autos, trucks, parts, and steel remains the medium-term CAD overhang. No diplomatic off-ramp is visible. The FOMC's September 16 hike to 3.75-4.00% (now 12-0, confirmed) and a December hike being priced add a second USD tailwind to USDCAD that was only partially priced during the prior week.

implications.CAD: MAXIMUM structural CAD negative from tariff war — US Section 338 50% tariffs live since Aug 22, Canada 700+ line retaliation live since Sep 8, Trump federal-contracts ban unrevoked, zero diplomatic off-ramp, Jan 1 2027 50% auto tariff threat. Oil CAD tailwind has weakened: WTI pulled back from $106 peak to ~$93.93 as of Sep 21 — significantly below the $100 level that had been capping USDCAD. Net directional bias is now more clearly USDCAD bullish with oil declining. BoC Oct 28 is the next policy binary — stagflationary dilemma (labor -41,700 Aug, tariff inflation pass-through) could produce dovish cut that accelerates CAD weakness.
implications.USD: FOMC confirmed 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00% on Sep 16 (12-0 unanimous). Dot plot year-end median 4.1-4.4% implies December hike is the base case. USD broadly supported by the Warsh tightening cycle. USDCAD directionally bullish on dual drivers: tariff war fundamentals and USD rate support. Oil pullback to ~$94 removes key CAD offset.
implications.MXN: USMCA credibility damage from US-Canada rupture keeps uncertainty elevated for Mexico. US-Mexico bilateral divergence from US-Canada adds structural MXN uncertainty premium.
implications.EUR: Indirect — EURCAD likely bid on structural CAD weakness. Broader protectionism signal from Section 338 invocation has limited but non-zero EUR contagion via global trade uncertainty.
implications.AUD: Commodity-bloc — AUD partially tied to oil/commodity complex. WTI pullback from $106 to ~$94 is mildly AUD-negative at the margin but copper and iron ore dynamics dominate AUDUSD more directly. Subject to tariff-war risk-off and USD strength from post-FOMC hike regime.
implications.NZD: Same as AUD. NZDCAD vol elevated. NZD defensive in commodity-bloc risk-off episodes.
implications.GBP: GBPCAD directional trade on CAD structural weakness. GBP otherwise dominated by BoE path.
implications.JPY: CADJPY under dual pressure — CAD structural weakness from Section 338 tariff war plus JPY structural bid from BOJ normalization cycle now confirmed at 1.25% with Oct 29-30 next binary at ~90% hike odds.

themes.watchLevel: USDCAD — oil pullback to ~$93.93 (Sep 21 close) from $106 peak is removing the primary USDCAD cap. Key upside: 1.3900 resistance — clean daily close above 1.3900 opens 1.4017-1.4100 if oil stays below $97 and BoC Oct 28 is dovish. Key support: 1.3783 (Sep 8 low); sustained break below 1.3750 requires oil back above $103-105 sustained. FOMC hike to 3.75-4.00% confirmed (Sep 16) adds second USD tailwind — Dec hike in dots means USD broadly bid. Oil re-escalation above $105 (pipeline damage, Hormuz closure) = USDCAD trapped again below 1.3900; oil falling toward $85 = USDCAD accelerates toward 1.40+. BoC Oct 28 binary: dovish cut = USDCAD toward 1.4100; hawkish hold = USDCAD relief to 1.3800. Theme ends only on: (1) formal re-opening of US-Canada talks with credible framework, or (2) Trump executive action suspending Section 338.

themes.title: BOJ hiked to 1.25% Sep 18 (7-2) but Ueda non-committal — USDJPY pushed back above 157; Oct 29-30 BOJ next binary at ~90% hike odds; intervention regime at 160.00 intact; post-hike USD-JPY rate gap dominant driver
themes.summary: As of September 21, the BOJ September 18 hike has been delivered as universally expected but the JPY response was paradoxically negative: USDJPY pushed back above 157 after the decision, because the vote was 7-2 (board members Toichiro Asada and Ayano Sato dissented in favor of holding) and Governor Ueda offered no forward guidance or commitment to further hikes at the post-meeting press conference. The BOJ lifted its uncollateralized overnight call rate by 25 basis points to 1.25% — the highest level since 1995 and the sixth rate increase since the BOJ exited negative interest rate policy in March 2024. The BOJ's statement maintained the standard language that it aims to 'continue to raise the policy interest rate and adjust the degree of monetary accommodation,' but markets interpreted the 7-2 split and Ueda's reticence as signaling the BOJ is not ready for back-to-back hikes. The 10-year JGB yield fell 4.9 basis points after the decision and the Nikkei 225 rose 1.5%, further confirming the market's dovish read. The dominant near-term driver has therefore shifted from the Sep 18 hike binary to: (1) the persistent US-Japan rate differential with the Fed now at 3.75-4.00% versus BOJ at 1.25% — a 250bp gap that keeps carry trade attractive and USDJPY supported above 155-157; and (2) the BOJ October 29-30 meeting, which now carries approximately 90% market-implied hike odds per TONA futures (centralbank.watch), with a fresh Outlook Report due. The next policy-relevant data are Japanese wage figures and the Tokyo CPI print ahead of Oct 29-30. The MoF/BOJ coordinated intervention regime at 160.00 remains fully intact — markets are aware a run toward 160 could invite government action. A hawkish Outlook Report at Oct 29-30 could reignite JPY appreciation; more caution would keep the carry trade humming above 157.

implications.JPY: BOJ hiked to 1.25% (7-2) but Ueda's non-committal presser caused USDJPY to push back above 157 — 'sell the fact' JPY dynamic. The rate gap with the US (3.75-4.00% vs 1.25% = 250bp) remains the dominant USDJPY driver and keeps carry trade structurally attractive. Oct 29-30 BOJ next binary: hawkish Outlook Report + 25bp hike (~90% priced) = USDJPY drops toward 153-155; dovish hold or cautious guidance = USDJPY rally toward 159-160 and intervention risk. JGB 10-year yield fell on Ueda dovish read — watch for reversal as Oct hike odds remain elevated.
implications.USD: FOMC at 3.75-4.00% (Sep 16, 12-0) and Dec hike priced means the USD-JPY rate differential is widening from the US side simultaneously with BOJ hiking — but the pace of Fed tightening relative to BOJ keeps USDJPY elevated. DXY broadly supported by Warsh tightening cycle.
implications.EUR: EURJPY under dual pressure — BOJ normalization cycle intact at 1.25% with Oct 29-30 next hike (~90% odds) vs ECB on hold. JGB yields structurally rising (though dipped on Ueda dovish read). Medium-term EUR-JPY rate differential narrowing.
implications.GBP: GBPJPY — Sep 18 BOJ hike delivered but dovish read limits near-term JPY upside. Oct 29-30 is the next directional catalyst for JPY crosses.
implications.CHF: CHFJPY under BOJ normalization pressure. SNB in easing mode adds divergence — CHFJPY structurally lower over medium term.
implications.CAD: CADJPY under dual pressure — CAD structural weakness from Section 338 tariff war plus JPY structural bid from BOJ normalization cycle (1.25% delivered, Oct 29-30 at ~90% hike odds).
implications.AUD: AUDJPY — Sep 18 BOJ hike delivered but Ueda dovish presser provided near-term relief. Oct 29-30 BOJ binary is next AUDJPY downside catalyst if hawkish Outlook Report confirms another 25bp.
implications.NZD: Same dynamic as AUD. NZDJPY under BOJ normalization structural pressure. Oct 29-30 binary dominant.

themes.watchLevel: USDJPY ~157+ as of Sep 21 — pushed above 157 on Ueda's non-committal presser post-Sep 18 hike. Key resistance: 158.50 (psychological); 160.00 is the hard intervention ceiling — MoF/BOJ coordinated US-Japan intervention remains on record; a run toward 160 is expected to trigger verbal or direct intervention. Key support: 156.50; 155.00 (major round number); 153.00 (post-BOJ hike downside target if Oct 29-30 Outlook Report is hawkish). Oct 29-30 BOJ binary: 25bp hike with hawkish Outlook Report (~90% TONA-implied) = USDJPY drops toward 153-155; no hike or cautious guidance = USDJPY rally toward 159-160 and intervention regime maximally tested. Watch Tokyo CPI and Japanese wage data ahead of Oct 29-30 as the primary pre-meeting signal. Theme invalidated: USDJPY sustained above 160.00 with MoF disclaimer = intervention regime broken; USDJPY below 150.00 = structural JPY bull trend in new leg requiring theme re-characterization.

themes.title: Post-dual-hike regime: Fed at 4.00% with Dec hike priced (dot median 4.1-4.4%); Warsh tightening cycle driving DXY; Dec FOMC and Nov 5 PCE are next USD binaries; G10 rate divergence reshaping all USD pairs
themes.summary: As of September 21, the September 16 FOMC decision has closed the pre-meeting binary and opened a new regime: the US is now tightening at the fastest pace since 2022, with the fed funds rate at 3.75-4.00% following a unanimous 12-0 vote, and the September dot plot showing year-end Fed funds projections between 4.1% and 4.4% — effectively pre-committing the committee to a December hike barring a material data reversal. Markets have moved to price approximately one additional 25bp hike in December 2026, with rate hike expectations extending into 2027 as well. Chair Warsh's inflation-fighting framework — validated by August CPI core +0.3% MoM, August payrolls three times consensus at +162,000, and oil structurally above $90 even after the mid-week pullback from $106 — is now in full institutional execution mode. The statement cited 'inflation remains elevated' and 'today's policy action will support a timelier return to the Committee's 2 percent goal.' The post-FOMC USD reaction was constructive: EURUSD moved below 1.1300, GBPUSD under pressure, and AUDUSD retreating toward 0.69. 10-year Treasury yields are surging with upward momentum. The new dominant themes are: (1) whether December's FOMC hike to 4.25% becomes fully priced — the next key data inputs are the October PCE (due early November), October CPI (due mid-November), and November FOMC (November 5 — hold expected but guidance critical); (2) G10 rate divergence from the Warsh tightening cycle against central banks on hold or easing (ECB, RBA, RBNZ); and (3) the oil wildcard — WTI at ~$93.93 (down from $106 peak) is an upside inflation risk that keeps the Dec hike case structurally intact even as it provides some commodity-currency relief. Treasury 10-year yields are the daily FX signal for this theme — sustained above 4.85% implies December hike is fully priced and DXY targets 101-102.

implications.USD: Broadly bullish. Fed at 3.75-4.00% (Sep 16, 12-0), dot plot 4.1-4.4% year-end implies Dec hike. DXY supported by highest Fed funds rate since 2023 and Warsh credibility. Next key levels: DXY 101-102 if Dec hike fully priced; 10yr UST sustained above 4.85% = confirmation. Nov 5 FOMC guidance and Oct PCE/CPI are the primary data triggers.
implications.EUR: EURUSD bearish — ECB on hold while Fed hikes. EURUSD moved below 1.1300 post-Sep 16 FOMC. Rate differential widening structurally USD-positive vs EUR. Next key level: 1.1200-1.1250 support; a sustained break below 1.1200 opens 1.1000 area. ECB Oct meeting could provide temporary EUR relief if hawkish surprise.
implications.GBP: GBPUSD under pressure from Fed-BoE divergence. BoE has its own inflation dynamics but the Fed rate advantage is structurally USD-positive. GBPUSD below 1.3400 is next key target if Dec Fed hike fully priced.
implications.JPY: USDJPY above 157 — Fed at 4.00% vs BOJ at 1.25% is a 275bp rate gap that keeps carry trade structurally attractive. Post-dual-hike regime means both central banks are tightening but at different speeds; the gap is widening from the US side faster. USDJPY upside capped by intervention at 160.00.
implications.CAD: USDCAD bullish from dual drivers — tariff war fundamentals plus USD rate advantage from Fed at 4.00% with Dec hike priced. Oil pullback to ~$94 from $106 removes the primary USDCAD cap. BoC Oct 28 policy binary adds third driver.
implications.AUD: AUDUSD bearish — RBA on hold while Fed hikes creates rate differential headwind. AUDUSD retreating toward 0.69 post-FOMC. Commodity support from elevated oil/metals provides partial offset but insufficient against Fed rate advantage.
implications.NZD: NZDUSD bearish — RBNZ rate path less hawkish than Fed. Same dynamic as AUD. NZDUSD toward 0.5800 area on Dec hike pricing.
implications.CHF: USDCHF bullish — SNB in easing mode while Fed at 4.00% hiking. CHF safe-haven partial offset on risk-off episodes but the rate divergence is structurally USDCHF positive.

themes.watchLevel: DXY and 10yr UST are the daily signal for this theme. 10yr UST: sustained above 4.85% = Dec hike fully priced, DXY targets 101-102; pullback below 4.60% = Dec hike doubts emerging, USD gives back gains. EURUSD: 1.1200-1.1250 is next support; break = Dec hike fully priced; bounce above 1.1400 = Dec hike doubt/risk-off USD selling. Key data calendar: October PCE (early Nov), October CPI (mid-Nov), November 5 FOMC (hold expected, guidance critical), December FOMC (live hike meeting). Oil wildcard: WTI re-escalation above $105 (Middle East pipeline/Hormuz) = inflation upside keeps Dec hike firmly priced AND provides partial AUD/CAD commodity bid creating cross-currency divergence; oil below $85 = inflation fears ease, Dec hike odds drop and USD bulls face headwinds. Theme retires: Dec FOMC decision resolves the binary; or a 3+ consecutive months of soft CPI/PCE that pushes Dec hike odds below 30%.
